name: Detector pilot
purpose: First test of a general AI-text detector trained on true origin (who produced the wording), not on Detector A scores. Question: can it catch humanized AI text that Detector A misses while leaving human text alone?
written_before_results_at: 2026-11-18, while the Wikipedia fetch and matched-AI generation were still running; no Detector had been trained or scored

baselines_measured_before_training.joint_holdout_detector_a: AUC by true origin 0.9588; flags 2/75 human (score > 0), catches 70/75 AI
baselines_measured_before_training.humanized_set_detector_a_flags_score_abo: AI originals 22/30, Humanizer B rewrites 4/30, Rewriter greedy rewrites 11/30

human_0: Wikipedia paragraphs from revisions saved on or before 2021-12-31 (fetch_wiki_human.py; Level-4 vital articles, 48 per area, every joint-holdout page excluded)
ai_1: ai_raw_wiki: paragraphs on the same Wikipedia titles written by llama3, qwen2.5:14b and the unadapted Qwen3-1.7B, each aimed at the word count of one human paragraph (gen_ai_matched.py)
ai_humanized_rewriter_wiki: the live Rewriter's rewrite of one of those per article
ai_raw_qwen3: master sources with collection_kind detector_a_only_import
ai_raw_chapter: master sources with source_type ai_written_chapter_user_declared or ai_written_book_user_declared
ai_raw_agent: master sources with source_origin agent_authored_textbook
ai_rewrite_base_qwen3: master sources with source_origin unadapted_base_qwen3 or unadapted_base_qwen3_academic_register
ai_humanized_rewriter: master sources with source_origin trained_qwen3_humanizer
ai_humanized_humanizer_b: collected or unassigned master outputs with humanization_source Humanizer B whose source is AI-origin
ai_humanized_humanizer_b_of_human: the same for Gutenberg sources; labelled AI because an AI rewriter produced the wording
excluded: Master sources with no origin evidence (no collection_kind, source_type or source_origin) and their outputs
Every text in the 30 source families of dataset-runs/rewriter-vs-humanizer-b-20261111 (evaluation set)
The 200 texts of the frozen Model 2 test split
Any text matching the joint holdout (verify.py must report 0 matches)
Normalized duplicates (one kept); a text that appears under both labels is dropped entirely

splits.unit: family: one Wikipedia article (its human, AI and rewritten paragraphs together), or one existing master group_id (a source with all its rewrites)

architecture: Same as Scorer-1H: [CLS] -> fresh dense+tanh pooler -> dropout 0.1 -> linear(1); reference SentencePiece tokenizer (model2-encoder-finetune-20261101/common.py)

training.schedule: linear warmup then linear decay to 0
training.loss: Binary cross-entropy on the logit with hard 0/1 origin labels, unweighted
training.sampling: Uniform reshuffle of all training texts each epoch
training.validation_during_training: End of each epoch, for curves only
training.checkpoint_selection: None: final weights after the fixed budget are the evaluated model

threshold: Fixed once, from validation only: the lowest score t such that at most 5% of validation human texts score above t. A text is flagged when its score is above t. The same t is used on every test set.
evaluation_order: 1. validation: AUC, threshold t, catch rate by AI type
2. detector-test (held-out Wikipedia articles): human false-alarm rate, catch rate by AI type
3. humanized set (rewriter-vs-humanizer-b-20261111): flags on 30 AI originals, 30 Humanizer B rewrites, 30 Rewriter greedy rewrites, 28 best-of-4 picks, against Detector A's own flags (score > 0)
4. unseen human source: about 200 arXiv abstracts submitted before 2022 (fetch_arxiv_human.py), never used in training; false-alarm rate
5. joint holdout, once, last: AUC by origin, human flagged, AI caught, against Detector A

positive_only_if_all: joint holdout: at most 7 of 75 human paragraphs flagged, and at least 60 of 75 AI paragraphs caught
humanized set: at least 15 of 30 Humanizer B rewrites caught (Detector A 4) and at least 20 of 30 Rewriter greedy rewrites caught (Detector A 11)
detector-test: at most 10% of held-out Wikipedia human paragraphs flagged
unseen human source: at most 15% of arXiv abstracts flagged
verdict_frozen_before_results.otherwise: Not a positive result. Everything is reported either way; nothing is retuned against the humanized set, the arXiv set or the joint holdout.

known_limits_before_results: Human training text comes from two sources (Wikipedia, five Gutenberg authors). The arXiv set is the only check on other human writing.
Humanizer B and the Rewriter are both seen in training (other families). Nothing here tests a humanizer the Detector has never seen.
Local generators are small or mid-size open models; the joint-holdout AI half (claude-opus-5-5) is the main check on a stronger generator.
Chapter and book sources are AI-written by the user's declaration, not independently verified.
